text.p: U.S. airliner Continental Airlines Inc said Friday it had completed a $707.3 million private placement of pass-through certificates to finance part of the cost of buying new aircraft.
The airliner said the placement will help finance the debt portion of the acquisition cost of up to 30 new Boeing Co aircraft.

"Pending the delivery of the aircraft, the net proceeds will be deposited with a financial institution for the benefit of the certificate holders," it said, adding that Boeing is scheduled to deliver the aircraft between March 1997 and February 1996.
A Continental spokeswoman said the financing and the order is part of a deal that the airliner reached with Boeing last October to buy a total of 60 737-500 and -600 aircraft.
The airliner said separate pass-through trusts had issued the certificates. The trusts will acquire equipment notes to be issued in connection with the financing of the aircraft, it added.

"The pass through certificates consist of $437.9 million of 7.461 percent Class A certificates, $148.3 million of 7.461 percent Class B certificates, $111.1 million of 7.420 percent Class C-I certificates, and $10 million of 7.420 percent Class C-II certificates," it said.
The certificates represent pooled debt obligations repackaged as shares.
